goal: Seven of twelve 600 s idle envelopes of pilot night qpe01-pilot-n1-20260922-0217 lost their clock anchor (the derived mapping from the power sampler's timestamps onto the host wall clock) because macOS's time daemon slewed the wall clock by 4 to 22 ms at its ~30 min NTP syncs and ran it at up to 7.6 ppm frequency correction between them, while derive_powermetrics_anchor_v3 (joulewise/uncertainty_evidence.py:35, :41) refuses any capture whose wall-minus-monotonic offset span or effective bound exceeds 5 ms absolute regardless of capture length. A 22 ms edge error on a 480 s interior at 0.32 W moves about 7 mJ, two orders below the ~1 J attribution limit and the 1.45 J envelope scatter. The method's docstring presumes an authenticated network-time-OFF admission that the evidence-night entry point never established (every session.json carries network_time_provenance null), and with NTP off the kernel's residual frequency correction alone (7.6 ppm = 4.5 ms per 600 s) still fails the absolute bound. Assemble the cold-gate packet (options: caps derived from the energy budget or scaled with capture length; an honest error bound pricing the observed slew into error_bound_j instead of refusing; a shorter anchored sub-interval per envelope; and, for the environment half, either an entry-point refusal when network time is ON or Ed's admin action to turn it OFF for windows, noting the residual-frequency point) together with the 1 us span_mismatch tolerance that left three bounded envelopes unretained, then implement the ruled option.
